writeup: TIC 313386191 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 40.7 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 3.32% dimming, and a secondary eclipse was detected at 5.5 sigma significance. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 11.1. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. One data quality flag warrants attention: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the initial automated period estimate was half the true orbital period. This systematic difference does not affect the pixel-level confirmation or timing measurements, and the corrected period of 40.7 days is reported here.
